recipes.title: Authentic Silken Miso Soup
recipes.description: A delicate and probiotic-rich staple of the Japanese diet. This soup features silky tofu and umami-packed dashi, prepared carefully to preserve the health benefits of the miso paste.

ingredients.displayName: Silken Tofu, diced into 1/2 inch cubes

instructions: In a medium saucepan, bring the dashi broth to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Do not let it reach a rolling boil.
Add the rehydrated wakame seaweed and the diced tofu to the broth. Simmer gently for 1-2 minutes until the tofu is warmed through.

Reduce the heat to the lowest setting. Place the miso paste into a small mesh strainer and dip it into the broth. Use a spoon to whisk the miso through the strainer into the liquid until fully dissolved. This ensures no clumps remain.
Remove the pan from the heat immediately. Do not boil the soup after adding miso, as high heat destroys its beneficial probiotics and delicate flavor.
Ladle into small bowls and garnish with fresh green onions. Serve hot.

recipes.title: Ginger-Soy Chicken Teriyaki
recipes.description: A healthy, pan-seared version of the classic Japanese dish. The chicken is glazed in a homemade, low-sugar ginger-honey sauce for a perfect balance of sweet and savory.
instructions: Pat the chicken thighs completely dry with paper towels. Lightly season both sides with a pinch of salt.
In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, mirin, honey, grated ginger, and minced garlic to create the teriyaki glaze.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Place the chicken in the pan and sear for 5-6 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
Remove the chicken from the pan and let it rest on a cutting board for 3 minutes. Wipe any excess oil out of the skillet.
Pour the teriyaki sauce into the same skillet and simmer over medium heat for 2-3 minutes until it reduces into a thick, glossy syrup.
Slice the chicken into 1/2 inch strips, return them to the pan, and toss thoroughly to coat in the glaze.
Serve hot over steamed brown rice or fresh greens.

recipes.title: Chilled Zaru Soba (Buckwheat Noodles)
recipes.description: A refreshing and high-fiber meal featuring 100% buckwheat noodles. This cold dish is a Japanese summer classic, perfect for a light and nutrient-dense lunch.
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add the soba noodles and cook according to package directions (usually 4-5 minutes). Do not overcook.
Drain the noodles and immediately plunge them into a large bowl of ice-cold water.
Gently rub the noodles with your hands under the cold water to remove the surface starch. This is essential for a clean, non-sticky texture.
Drain thoroughly and arrange on a bamboo tray or a flat plate. Sprinkle the shredded nori seaweed on top.
Prepare individual cups of chilled mentsuyu dipping sauce.
To eat, mix small amounts of wasabi and chopped green onions into your sauce cup. Dip a bite-sized portion of noodles into the sauce and enjoy.

recipes.title: Miso-Glazed Black Cod (Saikyo Yaki)
recipes.description: A world-renowned Japanese seafood dish. The buttery texture of the black cod is enhanced by a slow marination in a sweet and savory white miso paste.
instructions: In a small bowl, whisk together the white miso, mirin, and sake until it forms a smooth paste.
Coat the fish fillets generously on all sides with the miso mixture. Place in a shallow dish, cover, and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 6 hours (up to 48 hours for the deepest flavor).
Preheat your broiler to high.
Gently wipe off the excess miso from the fish with your fingers or a paper towel. Do not rinse the fish; you want a very thin layer remaining.
Place the fillets on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Broil 4-5 inches from the heat for 8-10 minutes. The top should develop charred spots and the fish should be buttery and flaky. Serve with a wedge of lemon.

recipes.title: Healthy Agedashi Tofu
recipes.description: A pan-seared version of the classic deep-fried appetizer. Firm tofu cubes are lightly coated in starch and served in a warm, savory dashi broth with fresh ginger.
instructions: Wrap the tofu block in paper towels and place a heavy plate on top for 15 minutes to press out excess water.
In a small saucepan, bring the dashi, soy sauce, and mirin to a simmer. Turn off the heat and keep the broth warm.
Cut the pressed tofu into 1.5-inch cubes.
Dredge each tofu cube in potato starch until fully coated, shaking off any excess. You want a very thin layer.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Pan-fry the tofu cubes for 2-3 minutes per side until a thin, crispy shell forms.
Place the hot tofu cubes into shallow bowls. Pour the warm broth around the base (not over the top) to keep the crust crispy.
Garnish with a small mound of grated ginger and fresh scallions.

recipes.title: Classic Oyakodon (Chicken & Egg Bowl)
recipes.description: A comforting 'parent-and-child' rice bowl. Tender chicken and onions are simmered in a savory dashi broth and finished with a layer of creamy, soft-set egg.
instructions: In a small skillet, combine the dashi, soy sauce, and mirin. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Add the sliced onions and cook for 2-3 minutes until they begin to soften.
Add the chicken pieces in a single layer. Simmer for 4-5 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked.
Pour the beaten egg slowly over the chicken and onions in a circular motion.
Cover the skillet and cook for 45-60 seconds until the egg is just set but still slightly moist.
Carefully slide the entire mixture onto a bowl of hot brown rice. Garnish with a sprinkle of fresh greens.

recipes.title: Salmon Shioyaki (Salt-Grilled Salmon)
recipes.description: The quintessential Japanese breakfast fish. Fresh salmon is salt-cured briefly to draw out moisture and then grilled until the skin is perfectly blistered and the flesh is tender.
instructions: Pat the salmon fillets dry with paper towels. Sprinkle salt generously on both sides.
Let the fish sit at room temperature for 15-20 minutes. This draws out excess moisture for a crispier skin.
Wipe away any beaded moisture with a clean paper towel.
Heat a grill pan or non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Place the salmon skin-side down.
Cook for 4-5 minutes until the skin is dark golden and crispy. Flip and cook for another 3-4 minutes until just opaque in the center.
Serve with a side of grated daikon (squeeze out some liquid) and a fresh lemon wedge.

recipes.title: Healthy Vegetable Okonomiyaki
recipes.description: A 'as-you-like-it' savory pancake packed with fiber-rich cabbage. This version uses whole wheat flour and is pan-steamed for a light, fluffy texture.
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, dashi, and eggs until smooth.
Fold in the shredded cabbage, green onions, and pickled ginger until every strand of cabbage is lightly coated.
Heat a teaspoon of oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Pour half the batter into the pan and shape into a circle about 1-inch thick. Do not press down.
Cook for 5-6 minutes until the bottom is browned. Flip carefully.
Cover the pan with a lid and cook for another 5 minutes to steam the cabbage through.
Serve topped with a thin drizzle of tonkatsu sauce and a dollop of Greek yogurt.

recipes.title: Simmered Hijiki Seaweed with Carrots
recipes.description: A traditional side dish (ish) rich in minerals and fiber. Rehydrated black seaweed is simmered with sweet carrots and a savory-sweet glaze.
instructions: Soak the dried hijiki in plenty of water for 20 minutes. Drain and rinse thoroughly.
Sauté the julienned carrots in a small pot with a drop of oil for 2 minutes.
Add the drained hijiki and stir-fry for another minute.
Add 1 cup of dashi (or water), soy sauce, mirin, and honey.
Simmer over medium-low heat until the liquid is almost entirely evaporated (about 12-15 minutes).
Let cool to room temperature before serving. This dish keeps well in the fridge.

recipes.title: Cold Tofu with Grated Ginger (Hiyayakko)
recipes.description: The simplest and most refreshing Japanese appetizer. Cold silken tofu is topped with pungent ginger and scallions to highlight its clean, creamy flavor.
instructions: Drain the silken tofu and carefully pat dry with a paper towel.
Cut the block into two large cubes and place each in a small chilled dish.
Top each cube with a small mound of freshly grated ginger and a sprinkle of minced green onions.
Drizzle with a tiny amount of soy sauce just before serving. Eat while very cold.

recipes.title: Simmered Kabocha Squash
recipes.description: A traditional Japanese vegetable dish. Sweet kabocha squash is simmered with its skin on to preserve nutrients and create a beautiful contrast in textures.
instructions: Wash the squash thoroughly. Leave the skin on, but scrape out the seeds. Cut into 1-inch chunky pieces.
Place the squash skin-side down in a single layer in a large pot.
Add the dashi, soy sauce, sugar, and salt. The liquid should cover about half the squash.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low. Place a lid directly on top of the squash pieces (or use a drop-lid) to distribute heat evenly.
Simmer for 12-15 minutes until the squash is tender when pierced with a fork. Let it cool slightly in the liquid before serving to let the flavors absorb.

recipes.title: Onigiri (Rice Triangles with Tuna)
recipes.description: A portable and healthy snack. Warm rice is shaped by hand into triangles and filled with a savory mixture of tuna and healthy yogurt.
instructions: In a small bowl, mix the drained tuna with Greek yogurt and a pinch of salt until well combined.
Wet your hands with water and sprinkle a small amount of salt over your palms.
Take about 1/2 cup of warm rice and create a small indentation in the center.
Place 1 teaspoon of the tuna mixture into the hole. Carefully close the rice around it to cover the filling.
Gently press the rice into a triangle shape using your palms. Do not squeeze too hard.
Wrap a strip of nori around the bottom center of the triangle. Repeat for the remaining rice.

recipes.title: Sukiyaki-Style Beef & Tofu
recipes.description: A lightened version of the classic hot pot. Thinly sliced lean beef and firm tofu are simmered with leafy greens in a sweet-savory broth.
instructions: In a large skillet or shallow pot, bring the dashi, soy sauce, and a tablespoon of honey to a simmer.
Add the sliced onions and mushrooms. Cook for 3 minutes until the onions soften.
Add the tofu cubes and continue simmering for another 3 minutes.
Arrange the beef slices in a single layer in the remaining space. Simmer for only 2-3 minutes until the beef is just cooked through (do not overcook).
Serve hot as a complete one-pot meal.

recipes.title: Spinach Goma-ae (Sesame Dressing)
recipes.description: A nutrient-packed side dish where blanched spinach is tossed in a rich, nutty paste of freshly toasted and ground sesame seeds.
instructions: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes until fragrant and golden. Grind the warm seeds in a mortar and pestle until they are mostly crushed.
Stir the soy sauce and honey into the ground seeds to form a thick paste.
Blanch the spinach in boiling water for exactly 60 seconds. Drain and plunge into ice water to stop the cooking.
Squeeze the spinach as dry as possible with your hands. Cut into 2-inch logs.
Toss the spinach thoroughly with the sesame paste until every leaf is coated. Serve chilled.

recipes.title: Steamed White Fish with Ginger
recipes.description: A light and elegant preparation that highlights the freshness of the fish. Steaming with ginger and sake creates a delicate broth and tender texture.

ingredients.displayName: White fish fillets (Cod or Sea Bass)

instructions: Pat the fish fillets dry and place them in a shallow, heat-proof dish.
Scatter the ginger strips over the fish and drizzle with sake and light soy sauce.
Set up a steamer basket over a pot of boiling water. Place the dish into the basket, cover, and steam over high heat for 10-12 minutes.
The fish is done when it is opaque and flakes easily with a fork.
Garnish with fresh green onions and serve immediately with the steaming juices poured over the top.

recipes.title: Healthy Yakisoba (Stir-Fry Noodles)
recipes.description: A lightened-up version of the classic street food. We use extra cabbage and lean protein, with a homemade sauce that’s low in sugar.
instructions: In a small bowl, whisk together the Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, and a dash of honey to make the yakisoba sauce.
Heat a non-stick wok or large skillet over high heat. Sear the chicken strips for 3 minutes until cooked through. Remove and set aside.
Add the cabbage and carrots to the same pan. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until the vegetables are slightly softened but still crisp.
Add the yakisoba noodles and 2 tablespoons of water. Cover the pan for 1 minute to steam and loosen the noodles.
Add the chicken and sauce back into the pan. Toss everything together for 2 minutes until the sauce is evenly distributed and the noodles are slightly caramelized.
Serve hot, garnished with pickled ginger (beni shoga).

recipes.title: Mizutaki (Chicken Hot Pot)
recipes.description: A healthy, one-pot dish where ingredients are simmered in a light kombu broth. Each bite is dipped in refreshing ponzu sauce for a clean and satisfying meal.
instructions: Fill a large pot with 4 cups of water and a piece of kombu (dried kelp). Let soak for 30 minutes, then bring to a near-boil.
Remove the kombu just before the water boils. Add the chicken cubes and simmer for 5 minutes, skimming off any foam that rises to the top.
Add the napa cabbage, mushrooms, and tofu. Simmer for another 10-15 minutes until the chicken is tender and vegetables are soft.
Serve the pot at the center of the table. To eat, dip individual pieces into small bowls of fresh ponzu sauce.

recipes.title: Japanese Rice Porridge (Okayu)
recipes.description: A gentle and comforting porridge often eaten for breakfast or when feeling unwell. It is remarkably easy on the stomach and highly hydrating.
instructions: Rinse the rice several times until the water runs clear. Drain thoroughly.
Place the rice and 2.5 cups of water in a heavy pot. Bring to a boil over medium heat.
Once boiling, reduce the heat to the lowest possible setting. Cover the pot and simmer for 30-40 minutes.
Check periodically; the rice should be very soft and have a creamy, thick consistency.
Stir in the salt. Ladle into bowls and place a salted plum (umeboshi) in the center of each. Garnish with scallions if desired.

recipes.title: Grilled Shiitake with Lemon-Soy
recipes.description: A simple way to enjoy the deep, earthy flavor of shiitake mushrooms. Grilling brings out their meatiness, while lemon and soy provide a bright finish.
instructions: Wipe the mushrooms clean with a damp cloth. Remove and discard the woody stems.
In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, lemon juice, and sake.
Heat a dry grill pan or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat.
Place the mushrooms in the pan, gills-side up. Cook for 3 minutes until they start to 'sweat'.
Flip the mushrooms and cook for another 2-3 minutes until they are tender and slightly charred.
Drizzle with the lemon-soy mixture while still in the pan, toss quickly, and serve hot.

recipes.title: Chawanmushi (Savory Egg Custard)
recipes.description: A delicate, silky steamed egg custard that melts in your mouth. This dish is seasoned with dashi and filled with small treasures of shrimp and mushrooms.
instructions: Gently whisk the eggs in a bowl. Avoid creating too many bubbles, as they will leave holes in the final custard.
Whisk in the dashi broth and light soy sauce. Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve twice to ensure a perfectly smooth texture.
Place two shrimp and a few slices of shiitake into the bottom of two individual ramekins or tea cups.
Carefully pour the egg mixture over the fillings until the cups are 3/4 full.
Cover the cups tightly with foil to prevent steam water from dripping in.
Place in a steamer over boiling water. Steam on medium heat for 2 minutes, then reduce to the lowest heat and steam for another 12 minutes.
The custard is done when it is set but still jiggles slightly like jelly. Serve hot.

recipes.title: Bean Sprout Namul
recipes.description: A crunchy and nutrient-dense side dish. Fresh bean sprouts are quickly blanched to preserve their snap and then seasoned with garlic and sesame oil.
instructions: Rinse the bean sprouts in cold water and remove any discolored ends.
Bring a pot of water to a boil. Blanch the sprouts for exactly 60 seconds.
Immediately drain and plunge into ice water. Squeeze out as much water as possible without crushing the sprouts.
In a small bowl, whisk together the sesame oil, minced garlic, and salt.
Toss the sprouts with the dressing until evenly coated. Serve chilled or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Daikon Salad with Plum Dressing
recipes.description: A crisp, hydrating salad featuring julienned daikon radish. The dressing uses traditional salted plums for a unique tart and savory flavor profile.
instructions: Cut the daikon into thin matchsticks (julienne). Soak them in ice water for 5 minutes to increase crunchiness, then drain and pat very dry.
To make the dressing: Mash the umeboshi plum into a paste and whisk with rice vinegar, honey, and a teaspoon of water.
Toss the daikon with the dressing in a large bowl.
Arrange on a plate and top with shredded nori and toasted sesame seeds just before serving.

recipes.title: Miso-Salmon en Papillote
recipes.description: A foolproof way to cook tender, juicy salmon. The fish is baked in a parchment paper pouch with vegetables and a savory miso glaze, steaming in its own juices.
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Whisk together the miso, honey, and a teaspoon of water to make a thin glaze.
Cut two large squares of parchment paper. Place a bed of sliced onions and mushrooms in the center of each.
Place a salmon fillet on top of the vegetables and brush generously with the miso glaze.
Fold the parchment paper over the fish and crimp the edges tightly to create a sealed pouch.
Bake on a sheet pan for 15 minutes. Carefully open the pouches (watch for steam!) and serve immediately.

recipes.title: Kimpira Gobo (Burdock Root)
recipes.description: A classic 'kinpira' (saute-and-simmer) dish. Burdock root and carrots are cut into matchsticks and glazed in a sweet soy sauce for a crunchy, earthy side.
instructions: Scrape the skin of the burdock root with the back of a knife. Cut into thin matchsticks and soak in water for 5 minutes (to prevent browning), then drain.
Heat the sesame oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Sauté the burdock matchsticks for 3 minutes.
Add the carrot matchsticks and sauté for another 2 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, honey, and 2 tablespoons of water. Simmer until the liquid is almost gone and the vegetables are glazed and tender-crisp.
Garnish with a sprinkle of red chili flakes (optional) and sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Japanese Potato Salad
recipes.description: A lighter take on a Japanese favorite. This potato salad is partially mashed for a unique texture and features crisp cucumbers and a tangy yogurt-based dressing.
instructions: Boil the potatoes until very soft. Drain and place in a bowl.
While hot, mash the potatoes roughly (leave some chunks). Stir in the rice vinegar and let cool.
Lightly salt the cucumber slices, let sit for 5 minutes, then squeeze out the water.
Blanch the diced carrots for 2 minutes and drain.
Mix the cooled potatoes with the cucumber, carrots, and Greek yogurt. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

recipes.title: Grilled Yellowtail Collar (Hamachi Kama)
recipes.description: The most prized and flavorful part of the yellowtail. The 'collar' is grilled until the skin is crispy and the inside is incredibly succulent and fatty.
instructions: Salt the yellowtail collar generously and let it sit for 10 minutes.
Preheat the broiler or grill to high. Place the collar skin-side up.
Grill for 12-15 minutes until the skin is charred and the fat has rendered. The meat should be tender and opaque.
Serve with a pile of grated daikon and a small bowl of ponzu for dipping.

recipes.title: Healthy Chicken Mizutaki
recipes.description: A light and cleansing hot pot dish. Chicken and plenty of leafy greens are simmered in a simple broth, focusing on the natural flavors of the ingredients.
instructions: Bring the broth to a simmer in a large pot. Add the chicken and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the cabbage, mushrooms, and tofu. Simmer for another 10-15 minutes until all ingredients are tender.
Serve in individual bowls with a splash of ponzu and a sprinkle of chopped scallions.

recipes.title: Steamed Pork & Ginger Dumplings
recipes.description: Delicate handmade dumplings filled with lean pork and fresh ginger. Steaming keeps them light and low in fat compared to pan-frying.
instructions: Combine pork, minced cabbage (squeezed dry), and ginger in a bowl.
Place 1 teaspoon of filling in each wrapper. Wet edges, fold and seal with pleats.
Place in a steamer basket lined with parchment. Steam over boiling water for 8 minutes.

recipes.title: Ginger-Soy Glazed Cod
recipes.description: A quick and nutrient-dense weeknight meal. Cod fillets are glazed in a bright ginger-soy reduction and baked until they melt in your mouth.
instructions: Mix ginger, soy sauce, and honey to make the glaze.
Brush the fish with the glaze and bake at 400°F for 10-12 minutes.
Baste once more halfway through cooking. Serve with steamed bok choy.

recipes.title: Warm Soba with Spinach & Tofu
recipes.description: A heart-healthy buckwheat noodle soup. Perfect for a quick, warm lunch that provides long-lasting energy and plant-based protein.
instructions: Cook soba noodles in boiling water, then drain.
Heat dashi in a pot. Add the tofu and spinach and simmer for 2 minutes until the spinach is wilted.
Add the cooked noodles to the pot and heat through. Season with a dash of soy sauce.

recipes.title: Grilled Eggplant with Sweet Miso (Nasu Dengaku)
recipes.description: A classic Japanese preparation of eggplant. The eggplant is grilled until soft and creamy, then brushed with a rich, sweet miso glaze.
instructions: Score the flesh of the eggplant in a diamond pattern.
Grill or pan-sear skin-side down first, then flesh-side down until tender.
Mix miso, sugar, and mirin to make a thick paste.
Brush the paste over the flesh of the eggplant and broil for 2 minutes until bubbly.

recipes.title: Healthy Vegetable Tempura (Baked)
recipes.description: All the crunch of traditional tempura without the deep-frying. Vegetables are lightly breaded and baked at high heat for a guilt-free treat.
instructions: Dip vegetable slices into whisked egg whites, then coat in panko.
Arrange on a baking sheet lined with parchment.
Bake at 425°F for 15-18 minutes until crispy and golden.

recipes.title: Shichimi Roasted Broccoli
recipes.description: A zesty and spicy broccoli side. Seasoned with 'Shichimi Togarashi' (7-spice powder) and roasted until the edges are crispy and caramelized.
instructions: Toss broccoli with oil and spice mix.
Roast at 400°F for 12 minutes until tender and slightly charred on the edges.

recipes.title: Udon Noodle Soup with Baby Bok Choy
recipes.description: A simple and comforting noodle soup. Thick, chewy udon noodles are served in a clean dashi broth with fresh green baby bok choy.
instructions: Bring dashi to a boil. Add udon noodles and cook for 3 minutes.
Add halved baby bok choy and simmer for 2 more minutes.
Serve hot with a dash of soy sauce and sesame oil.

recipes.title: Grilled Shrimp with Ginger-Garlic
recipes.description: Succulent grilled shrimp marinated in a potent ginger and garlic blend. A high-protein dish that's perfect for a quick and healthy dinner.
instructions: Marinate shrimp in ginger, garlic, and a teaspoon of soy sauce for 10 minutes.
Grill for 2 minutes per side until pink and opaque.
Garnish with fresh lemon and parsley.

recipes.title: Traditional Natto Rice Bowl
recipes.description: The breakfast of champions in Japan. Fermented soybeans (Natto) provide an incredible source of probiotics and protein, served over warm brown rice.
instructions: Stir the natto vigorously in a small bowl until it becomes very stringy and bubbly.
Mix in the provided sauce and mustard packets.
Pour over hot rice and top with fresh scallions.

recipes.title: Lite Beef & Broccoli Stir-Fry
recipes.description: A healthy Japanese-style stir-fry. We use very little oil and focus on a high vegetable-to-meat ratio with a savory soy-ginger sauce.
instructions: Sear beef strips in a very hot non-stick pan for 2 minutes. Remove.
Add broccoli and a splash of water to the pan. Cover and steam for 3 minutes.
Return beef to the pan, add soy sauce and ginger, and toss for 1 minute.

recipes.title: Shogayaki (Ginger Pork) Lite
recipes.description: One of Japan’s most popular home-cooked meals. Thinly sliced pork is seared and glazed with a pungent ginger sauce, traditionally served with shredded cabbage.
instructions: Whisk together ginger, soy sauce, and a dash of mirin.
Sear pork slices in a hot pan for 1 minute per side.
Pour the ginger sauce over the pork and simmer for 1 minute until glazed.
Serve with a mountain of shredded green cabbage.

recipes.title: Lemony Steamed Clams with Sake
recipes.description: A sophisticated and light seafood dish. Fresh clams are steamed in a bath of sake and lemon, creating a savory and aromatic broth.
instructions: Place clams, sake, and lemon in a large pot.
Cover and steam over high heat for 5-7 minutes until all clams have opened.
Discard any that stay closed. Garnish with chopped scallions.

recipes.title: Cucumber and Seaweed Sunomono
recipes.description: A simple version of the classic vinegar salad. This recipe focuses on the crispness of the cucumber and the mineral-rich wakame seaweed.
instructions: Soak seaweed in water for 5 mins.
Mix sliced cucumber with rice vinegar and a pinch of salt.
Toss with the drained seaweed and serve cold.

recipes.title: Grated Nagaimo with Soy
recipes.description: A unique Japanese texture experience. Mountain yam (Nagaimo) is grated into a silky, slippery foam and seasoned simply with soy sauce and nori.
instructions: Peel and grate the nagaimo into a bowl until it reaches a foamy consistency.
Add a dash of soy sauce and top with shredded nori. Serve as a cooling side dish.

recipes.title: Sesame Lemony Spinach
recipes.description: A fusion of flavors. Blanched spinach is tossed with toasted sesame seeds and a bright citrus dressing for a high-iron, zesty side.
instructions: Blanch spinach for 60 seconds, then drain and squeeze dry.
Toss with lemon juice, a drop of sesame oil, and toasted sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Steamed Carrot matchsticks with Ginger
recipes.description: Sweet carrots are steamed gently to preserve their natural sugars and then seasoned with warming fresh ginger.
instructions: Steam carrot strips for 5 minutes until tender-crisp.
Toss with fresh ginger and a tiny pinch of salt.

recipes.title: Grilled Red Snapper (Tai Shioyaki)
recipes.description: A celebratory dish in Japan. Whole or filleted red snapper is salt-grilled to highlight its naturally sweet and delicate white flesh.
instructions: Salt the fish and let it sit for 15 minutes.
Grill or broil for 5-6 minutes per side until the skin is crispy and meat is flaky.

recipes.title: Miso-Honey Roasted Radishes
recipes.description: An unusual but delicious way to enjoy radishes. Roasting removes their bite and turns them sweet, especially when glazed in a miso-honey sauce.
instructions: Toss radishes with a mixture of miso, honey, and a teaspoon of oil.
Roast at 400°F for 15 minutes until tender and glazed.

recipes.title: Cold Soba Salad with Miso Dressing
recipes.description: A high-fiber, plant-based lunch. Cold buckwheat noodles are tossed with raw vegetables and a creamy, nutrient-rich miso-sesame dressing.
instructions: Cook and chill soba noodles. Toss with julienned cucumber.
Whisk miso with rice vinegar and sesame oil to make the dressing.
Toss everything together and serve cold.

recipes.title: Sea Bass with Plum & Ginger
recipes.description: A light and zesty fish dish. Sea bass is steamed with tart salted plums and fresh ginger for a unique and sophisticated flavor profile.
instructions: Spread mashed plum and ginger over the fish fillets.
Steam over boiling water for 10-12 minutes until opaque.
Garnish with fresh green onions.

recipes.title: Healthy Vegetable Gyoza (Baked)
recipes.description: Handmade dumplings filled with a mixture of finely minced mushrooms and cabbage. Baked until the bottoms are golden and crispy.
instructions: Fill wrappers with vegetable mixture and seal with pleats.
Place on a baking sheet and brush the bottoms with a little oil.
Bake at 400°F for 15 minutes until the bottoms are crispy.

recipes.title: Lemony Japanese cucumber Salad
recipes.description: A bright and hydrating side. This version of Sunomono uses fresh lemon juice instead of rice vinegar for an extra citrusy kick.
instructions: Slice cucumber paper-thin. Toss with lemon juice and a tiny pinch of salt.
Let sit for 5 minutes and serve chilled.

recipes.title: Simmered Tofu with Kelp (Yudofu)
recipes.description: A very simple and warming dish from Kyoto. Blocks of silken tofu are gently heated in a kombu-infused water and served with savory dipping sauces.
instructions: Heat water with a piece of kombu. When small bubbles appear, add large cubes of tofu.
Simmer for 5 minutes (do not boil). Serve with a side of ponzu and ginger for dipping.
